# Membership lifecycle

The [membership resource](../resources/workspace_member.md) owns access for declared emails, not global user provisioning. Configure one active workspace per provider. Keep the verified automation identity, its roles, and a usable independent recovery administrator outside Terraform-managed resources.

## Known v2.44 teardown constraint

Destroying an accepted member and its Terraform-owned custom role is not fully supported on v2.44.0. The server removes membership but can retain its user-workspace ID in the role-assignment cache. The following role deletion then fails. The provider returns a fixed cache diagnostic, retains the role in state, and does not retry or rebind other users. The member can already be absent from both state and server while the role remains in both.

Inspect actual membership and retained role state. Combined teardown remains constrained until the upstream cache is refreshed or fixed. This pin has no verified safe Metadata-only cache refresh or tested repair procedure. Do not assume an immediate retry or server restart will resolve it.

## Roles and declared emails

Use managed-role references to create dependencies. Use the role data source for built-in roles and definitions owned elsewhere. The workspace data source confirms which workspace the provider binds; it does not select or create a workspace.

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.10"
  required_providers {
    twenty = {
      source = "glitchedmob/twenty"
    }
  }
}

# Unreleased provider. Use a locally built binary and CLI dev_overrides.
variable "twenty_endpoint" { type = string }
variable "twenty_email" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}
variable "twenty_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}
provider "twenty" {
  endpoint = var.twenty_endpoint
  email    = var.twenty_email
  password = var.twenty_password
}

# Role deletion needs ROLES, APPLICATIONS, and WORKSPACE_MEMBERS on the caller.
# External invitation references, including expired rows, block role deletion.
# Provision the verified operator and independent recovery admin outside Terraform.
# Omit both emails here. New emails receive invitations, not passwords.
variable "declared_members" {
  type = map(string)
  default = {
    "alice@example.com" = "triage"
    "bob@example.com"   = "member"
  }
  validation {
    condition = alltrue([
      for email, role in var.declared_members :
      email == lower(trimspace(email)) && contains(["triage", "member"], role)
    ])
    error_message = "Declare lowercase emails and select triage or member."
  }
}

data "twenty_workspace" "current" {}
data "twenty_role" "member" {
  label = "Member"
}
resource "twenty_role" "triage" {
  label                       = "Support triage"
  can_be_assigned_to_users    = true
  can_read_all_object_records = true
  permission_flags            = []
}
locals {
  member_role_ids = {
    triage = twenty_role.triage.id
    member = data.twenty_role.member.id
  }
}
resource "twenty_workspace_member" "declared" {
  for_each = var.declared_members
  email    = each.key
  role_id  = local.member_role_ids[each.value]
}
output "workspace_id" {
  value = data.twenty_workspace.current.id
}
```

Replace placeholder emails and inject ephemeral credentials at runtime. Do not commit real member maps, state, saved plans, credentials, or mail. State contains declared email identities and native member/invitation IDs, but never passwords or invitation links/tokens.

Only keys declared in `for_each` are managed. Removing one destroys its access. Other workspace members are left alone.

## Invitations and acceptance

Create sends one invitation and returns immediately. The recipient completes the normal server sign-in/onboarding flow outside Terraform. Acceptance preserves `workspaceUUID/email` as the resource ID. A fresh read records `accepted` and the native workspace-member UUID.

Pending role changes cancel and reissue. Expiration records `expired` and plans replacement. Old mail links stop working after revocation. Neither case waits for acceptance or sends mail during Read.

Existing pending, expired, or accepted access requires [explicit import](import.md). Import reads the actual role; it does not grant the configured role until a later apply. A legacy invitation with a null role resolves the current workspace default on read.

Role deletion inspects every stored invitation, not only declared emails. An explicit role reference blocks deletion even when expired or outside Terraform, so acceptance and membership reads are not stranded by a deleted role. Null roles follow the protected default. The caller needs `ROLES`, `APPLICATIONS`, and `WORKSPACE_MEMBERS`, or full-settings access, to delete a role; create and update keep their existing `ROLES` requirement. Terraform retains the role on read denial or malformed/incomplete invitation data and never cancels or rebinds invitations to unblock deletion. Deliberately revoke or replace external references through supported Twenty administration before deleting the role.

## External replacement and ownership

Revoking and recreating an invitation for the same email does not transfer Terraform ownership. The same rule applies to accepted-member removal/recreation. If a known native ID changes, refresh or update reconciliation records the replacement, clears `ownership_confirmed`, and returns a fixed warning. Further update/destroy operations refuse it until explicit inspection/import. Ordinary Read acceptance, or acceptance observed before any cancellation attempt, keeps confirmation and the compound ID. An unconfirmed binding never becomes confirmed just because refresh can see access.

Inspect the current access and match its role in configuration. Use `terraform state rm ADDRESS` to remove only the local binding, then import `workspaceUUID/email`. Neither operation revokes access. Review the next plan before applying.

## Partial failures

Invitation persistence happens before mail delivery in v2.44.0. A failed HTTP response, GraphQL error, or mail-send failure can therefore leave access on the server. The provider makes no blind retry. It records readable access and the stable ID, or retains `unconfirmed` when a read also fails.

A send is confirmed only after a valid single result and matching fresh reads. Otherwise `ownership_confirmed` remains false. A competing administrator could have created the visible invitation, so successful refresh alone cannot authorize takeover.

After a failure:

1. Restore list permissions or connectivity and inspect a fresh plan/state. Check delivery through your normal mail administration process; never copy tokens into Terraform.
2. If complete reads prove absence, refresh removes state. A later apply can send once.
3. If access remains with `ownership_confirmed = false`, match its current role in configuration. Remove only the local binding with `terraform state rm ADDRESS`, then explicitly import `workspaceUUID/email`. This does not revoke access.
4. Review any planned role change or replacement before applying. A failed create can be tainted. Import creates a new confirmed binding and avoids an automatic tainted replacement.

If ownership is already confirmed, repair the reported problem and review the next plan rather than sending again manually. Revocation can succeed while replacement fails; there may be no access to restore automatically. The provider does not roll back by deleting a member or an unrelated invitation.

If accepted access is first observed after a cancellation attempt, the operation fails without removing or changing it and clears `ownership_confirmed`. This applies even after successful cancellation: another administrator could have created a different invitation and the recipient could have accepted it before the follow-up snapshot. Twenty does not report which invitation created the member. A failed follow-up snapshot also clears confirmation while retaining the last readable attributes. Refresh cannot restore confirmation; inspect remaining access and explicitly import it using the recovery steps above before another update or destroy.

Acceptance observed before cancellation, or during an ordinary Read, keeps existing confirmation. Duplicate target invitations or members fail closed; resolve them through supported Twenty administration before continuing.

## Removal effects and limits

Destroy uses the server's `deleteUserFromWorkspace`, not raw member CRUD. The server can transfer connected-account ownership to its custodian, make workflow ownership/grants workspace-visible, and delete agent chat history for the removed member. If this was the user's only workspace, the server also soft-deletes the global user. Terraform does not own that global identity and cannot undo those cascades. Review removal as an access and data-retention change.

The provider prevents its own attempt to remove the final workspace member or independent full-settings administrator. Another administrator must retain a role with `can_update_all_settings = true` and user assignability. A subset of explicit settings flags is not counted as a full-settings administrator. These checks do not test the other administrator's password, MFA, or recovery process.

The combined teardown regression owns both resources in Terraform, accepts the server-issued invitation, and verifies an empty plan before destroy. On the pinned v2.44.0 server, destroy returns the classified role-cache failure. Fresh reads confirm membership is absent from state and server, the custom role remains in state and server, and both unmanaged administrators retain their identity and Admin assignment. There is one member deletion and one role deletion request, with no repair mutations. This is an expected upstream failure, not a successful combined lifecycle.

All lists used here are unpaginated in this pin. The lock shared by role and membership resources serializes one provider configuration only. There is no server transaction or conditional mutation. Pause other IAM writers and provider aliases during apply.
